computation.rule: per-package recency_score: 100 if days_since<=30; 90 if <=60; 75 if <=180; 60 if <=365; 30 if <=730; 0 otherwise. final score = arithmetic mean of per-package recency_scores.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.limitations: Release-date recency on Maven Central is a maintenance proxy, not a direct measure of code quality or issue-response time; some mature libraries (e.g. kotlinx.coroutines, kotlinx.serialization) intentionally ship less frequently once API-stable while still receiving continuous commit activity upstream, so the measured 100-180 day gaps likely understate true maintenance health for those specific packages. This proxy was collected identically for all languages in this evaluation.

methodology.raw_measure: days elapsed between each package's most recent Maven Central release (or, for Arrow/Kotest, most recent GitHub commit/dependency-bump activity) and the snapshot date
methodology.retrieval_route: mvnrepository.com Maven Central mirror release-date field; GitHub repository/organization activity pages
sampled_packages: Kotest (io.kotest, observed via arrow-kt/arrow-website dependency-bump PR)
methodology.selection_rule: Reuse of the same 8 domain-representative libraries selected under metric.third_party_library_availability_domain_coverage (excluding the JVM-interop-only logging entry), applied identically for maintenance-activity measurement to avoid introducing a second, independent sampling frame.

package_findings.evidence: Maven Central io.ktor group shows 'Last Release on Sep 17, 2026.'
arrow-kt/arrow's past-year commit-activity panel shows activity 'Updated Sep 1, 2026.'
A renovate-bot PR merged Sep 17, 2026 bumped 'io.kotest:kotest-property 6.2.1 to 6.2.5,' indicating an active recent Kotest release.

computation.adjustment: -4 points applied for domains with materially slower release cadence at snapshot time relative to the sampled median (CLI: 249 days since last release) and for reliance on smaller-team-maintained (non-JetBrains-core) packages in the functional-programming and logging domains, which increases single-maintainer risk relative to domains backed directly by JetBrains.
computation.rule: score = 100 * (weighted domain credit sum / number of domains), where each domain earns 1.0 credit if a Kotlin-native or first-class-multiplatform library exists with evidence of a release/commit within the last 12 months, 0.6 credit if only JVM-interop/Java-ecosystem coverage exists without a Kotlin-native option, 0 if no coverage evidence found.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations: Raw popularity indicators (stars, downloads) were not used as a standalone proxy; release-date recency from Maven Central was used as a declared, consistently-collected proxy for currency. Kotlin's full interop with the Java/Maven ecosystem is a structural strength not fully captured by this 10-domain sample; domains such as desktop GUI, ML/data-science, and embedded/bare-metal were excluded from the fixed sample and are comparatively less mature natively in Kotlin than in some other ecosystems.

methodology.candidate_universe_reproduction: kotlinlang.org/docs (serialization.html, coroutines docs, Ktor references); jetbrains.com/exposed; github.com/AAkira/Kotlin-Multiplatform-Libraries/wiki category lists (Network, Test, DI, Command Line Interface, etc.)
methodology.examination_depth: one official-docs check + one Maven Central release-metadata check per domain, identical depth applied across all assigned languages
methodology.retrieval_route: mvnrepository.com (Maven Central mirror) for release/version metadata; official project GitHub repositories/release pages; kotlinlang.org and jetbrains.com official docs/blog for domain-official designation
methodology.selection_rule: For each domain, select the library explicitly named in official Kotlin/JetBrains documentation (kotlinlang.org, jetbrains.com) where one exists (language-official designation, independent of benchmark outcome); otherwise select the top entry listed under the matching category of the community-curated 'Kotlin Multiplatform Libraries' wiki (github.com/AAkira/Kotlin-Multiplatform-Libraries), a category catalog maintained independently of this benchmark.
